challenge.geowords: three app-generated words per round from the approved review words of block 4 sections 1-7, three words from three different sections; letters on the countries map of North America with its rivers

prompt.object: the country or river name as on the cards; no capitals, records or facts

speedHunt.order: difficulty alternates easy, medium, easy, hard… (random inside a tier, no object repeats within a round); after a tier runs out the others go on in turn

islands.how: their tap areas are carried onto the countries map through the frame of the Caribbean map (the same base, tools/namerica_base.py)

speedHunt.correct: +1 and the next object at once
speedHunt.wrong: the right place lights up for 0.5 s; no penalty except time; the object goes into the weak list
speedHunt.hit: a river counts within 8 CSS px of its drawn line; a country counts inside its outline or within 22 CSS px of it; the small countries (the hard tier) within 36 CSS px — an enlarged tap area that lies only over the sea, never over a neighbour: a tap inside another country's outline answers that country (only a tap within 2 px of the asked country's own border line still counts for it), and the nearest object of the pool wins, so two enlarged areas never overlap

excluded.why: the eight small states of the Lesser Antilles cannot be seen on the map of the whole continent, even enlarged (Svetlana 18.11.2026: they are reviewed in lesson 3); lakes, mountains, deserts and section-1 places are on other maps; no capitals

speedHunt.score: objects found in the round + personal best

stars.note: the same as Europe and Asia; tune after testing with children

geowords.words: approved review words (role review) of data/dictionary/b4-section-1..7.json, each word once; three different sections per round; recently played words last
geowords.places: the countries map of North America (namerica-countries.webp): the 10 countries of section 6 (a letter in the main part of the country, its circle wholly inside the border; a country too small for that takes no letter), the 13 rivers («on the Mississippi») and a river inside a country it crosses, and the section-1 objects (seas, gulfs, peninsulas, islands, oceans); at least a third of the letters on rivers, then the other places first, so a word is never rivers only; a country named once; spacing 10% of map width
geowords.fallback: a word that cannot be laid out is replaced by the next word of another section
